convention: anthropics/skills/skill-creator evals.json per references/schemas.md. Every entry carries `should_trigger` so skill-creator's description-optimisation loop can score train/held-out trigger accuracy; the graded fixtures (ids 1-2 start-from-nothing, id 4 the empty-CLJS merge route, id 17 the generator route, id 18 a custom qualified project name on the manual route) additionally carry `expected_output` + `expectations[]` — graded answer-quality axes in the same shape as re-frame2-xray's Layer-2 evals — so routing AND outcome are both evaluated (rf2-rc0yh).
notes: Positives target greenfield re-frame2 bootstrap (empty dir, or shadow-cljs project with no re-frame2 wiring). Negatives target authoring on a working v2 project, v1 migration, live-runtime, or 'adding re-frame2 to an existing non-trivial app' (which is authoring, not setup). Execution contract (rf2-rc0yh): an unqualified greenfield request takes the ZERO-INTERVIEW default — Reagent, the generator template's pinned baseline as the version pin, the acme/my-app reference identity (namespace acme.my-app) / :app build id / port 8280 — and the skill EXECUTES: it writes the files, runs npm install, runs a terminating `npx shadow-cljs compile app`, starts the watch, and reports the URL without claiming the browser mounted from compile success alone. Both routes are the skill's to run: the manual scaffold is the default's exact-files path, and the `clojure -Tnew create …` generator is a complete alternative the skill runs itself when the author asks for it (allowed-tools cover -Tnew). setup_drift_test Lock 12 (pin-default-is-zero-interview + skill-executes-the-scaffold-and-reports-the-url) guards this contract; the default's twelve files are the generator template's own emission (references/first-counter.md, derived and drift-locked), so the manifest carries no schemas, Xray, devtools preload or CSP.

evals.name: start-from-nothing
evals.prompt: Start me a new re-frame2 ClojureScript project from an empty directory. I want deps.edn, shadow-cljs.edn, and a counter that mounts.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks no clarifying question. It writes the default Reagent project — the twelve files of references/first-counter.md, the generator template's own emission for acme/my-app: deps.edn (core + the Reagent adapter + reagent/reagent at the template's pinned baseline), package.json, shadow-cljs.edn, .gitignore, resources/public/index.html + css/app.css, src/acme/my_app/{core,events,subs,views}.cljs, test/acme/my_app/events_test.cljs, README.md — points the two day8/re-frame2* coordinates at the reviewed checkout (pre-publish), runs npm install and a terminating `npx shadow-cljs compile app` itself, starts the watch, and hands off with the successful command, the URL http://localhost:8280/, and an ask-the-author-to-click 0→1 line.
expectations: The response asks NO clarifying question — no version / substrate / devtools interview; it proceeds on Reagent with the generator template's pinned baseline as the pin.

The files written are the default twelve-file manifest — deps.edn, package.json, shadow-cljs.edn, .gitignore, resources/public/index.html (+ css/app.css), src/acme/my_app/{core,events,subs,views}.cljs, test/acme/my_app/events_test.cljs, README.md — with the day-one coords (core + -reagent + reagent/reagent; no -schemas, no -xray, no @xyflow/react / elkjs, no devtools preload, no CSP) at ONE pin and no unresolved <VERSION>/<SHA> placeholder left in any written file; pre-publish the two day8/re-frame2* coordinates are pointed at the reviewed checkout with :local/root before npm install.
The skill runs the commands itself — npm install, then a terminating `npx shadow-cljs compile app`, then starts `npx shadow-cljs watch app` — rather than telling the author which commands to run.

The handoff names the successful verification command and the served URL (http://localhost:8280/) and does NOT claim the counter mounted from compile success alone — it asks the author to open the page and click +1 (expecting 0→1).

evals.name: scaffold-cmd
evals.prompt: Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me.
evals.expected_output: The unqualified request takes the zero-interview default end to end: Reagent, template-baseline pin, the template's reference identity acme/my-app (namespace acme.my-app) / :app build id / port 8280, the twelve-file counter scaffold and nothing more; files written, coordinates pointed at the checkout, install + terminating compile executed by the skill, watch started, concise factual handoff with the URL and the single next skill (re-frame2).
expectations: The response takes the zero-interview default: no questions about version, substrate, name, or tooling — Reagent + the template-baseline pin, the acme/my-app reference identity, :app build id, port 8280.

A deterministic Reagent project is written — the twelve files of references/first-counter.md — with the day-one set (core + -reagent at ONE pin, plus an explicit reagent/reagent; nothing else: no schemas, Xray, Story, HTTP or CSP) and no placeholders.
Install and the terminating compile verification are executed by the skill (npm install; `npx shadow-cljs compile app` exit 0), with the watch started and the URL reported.
The handoff is concise and factual — files created, command verified, URL, and the single next skill (re-frame2) — with no option matrix, capability tour, or wizard.

evals.name: add-to-empty-cljs
evals.prompt: I have an empty CLJS project (shadow-cljs.edn exists, no re-frame2 yet). Add re-frame2 + Reagent and walk me to a working counter.
evals.expected_output: The agent MERGES into the files that exist rather than overwriting them, and it handles the shape this prompt actually describes: a shadow-cljs project whose classpath comes from shadow-cljs.edn's own :dependencies vector, with no deps.edn at all. Because shadow's resolver takes Maven coordinates only, and pre-publish the only re-frame2 coordinates that resolve are :local/root and :git/url, the agent converts the project to a deps.edn classpath instead of writing an unresolvable :mvn/version into :dependencies.
expectations: The agent establishes whether a deps.edn exists before adding coordinates to one — the prompt's 'shadow-cljs.edn exists' project ordinarily has none.

On the :dependencies-only project the agent CONVERTS: it writes a deps.edn carrying :paths (the author's existing source dirs), the day-one coords and a :shadow alias with the project's existing thheller/shadow-cljs version, then replaces shadow-cljs.edn's :dependencies with {:deps {:aliases [:shadow]}}.

The author's existing source dirs move into deps.edn in the same edit — app dirs on :paths, test dirs on the :shadow alias's :extra-paths. Once the classpath comes from deps.edn, shadow warns about and ignores shadow-cljs.edn's :source-paths, so a conversion that leaves a dir only there silently drops it off the classpath.

The agent does NOT write [day8/re-frame2 "0.0.1.alpha"] (or any :mvn/version framework coord) into :dependencies pre-publish — it 404s at resolution; the pre-publish shapes are :local/root or :git/url, which :dependencies cannot express.
The author's own :builds, mount-point id, dev-http port and :output-dir / :asset-path are preserved; the leaf's shapes are the target, not a literal overwrite.

evals.name: generator-route-in-empty-dir
evals.prompt: Use the generator to scaffold a UIx app in this empty directory.
evals.expected_output: The agent RUNS the generator itself from the author's empty directory and reports the real exit code and the emitted project. The `:local/root` it passes is the ABSOLUTE path of tools/template inside the reviewed re-frame2 checkout the skill was installed from (forward slashes, no hand-authored escaping) — never the literal relative "tools/template", which resolves under the author's own directory and dies `Local lib day8/re-frame2-template not found` before deps-new emits anything. The command's working directory stays the author's location, so the project lands there and not in the re-frame2 checkout. Pre-publish the emitted `deps.edn` carries framework coords that do not resolve, so the run continues into SKILL.md step 2 (the `:local/root` rewrite) and is reported against the emitted project's compile, not the generator's exit code alone.
expectations: The skill EXECUTES `clojure -Sdeps … -Tnew create … :substrate :uix` itself (the allowed-tools grant covers it) rather than printing the command for the author to run.
The `:local/root` passed is an ABSOLUTE path ending in tools/template, derived from the installed skill's own checkout location — not the literal relative "tools/template" and not a guessed path.

The command is NOT run from the re-frame2 checkout to make the dependency resolve: cwd stays the author's target location (or deps-new's :target-dir/:overwrite options are used), so the emitted project appears under the author's directory and no project files are written into the re-frame2 checkout.

The report names the generator's actual exit code and the emitted files (deps.edn, shadow-cljs.edn, package.json, the UIx entry namespace) — a failed or unrun generator is reported as such, never narrated as success.
If no reviewed re-frame2 checkout can be resolved on disk, the skill says so and falls back to the manual 6-step UIx path instead of guessing a template path.

Emission is not the finish line: pre-publish the skill applies SKILL.md step 2 to the emitted deps.edn — rewriting the two `day8/re-frame2*` `:mvn/version` coords to `:local/root` paths into the reviewed checkout — and then reports the emitted project's own `npx shadow-cljs compile app` result, not the generator's exit code alone. A generator that exits 0 into a project whose framework coords cannot resolve is reported as unfinished, never as success.

evals.name: custom-qualified-name-manual-scaffold
evals.prompt: Scaffold me a re-frame2 app called com.acme/my-cool-app.
evals.expected_output: The agent takes the manual (default) route and DERIVES the project identity before writing anything, instead of substituting `acme` / `my-app` token by token. The supplied coordinate `com.acme/my-cool-app` yields four different strings: the namespace root `com.acme.my-cool-app`, the source/test path `com/acme/my_cool_app` (dots become directory separators, dashes become underscores), the npm package name and project directory `my-cool-app` (the artefact segment alone), and the human label `com.acme/my-cool-app` kept verbatim in the `<h1>`, the `<title>` and the README heading. `shadow-cljs.edn`'s `:init-fn` is `com.acme.my-cool-app.core/init` and every internal require names the derived namespace. The run then finishes the way the default route finishes: SKILL.md step 2's coordinate rewrite, `npm install`, a terminating `npx shadow-cljs compile app` that exits 0, the watch started, and the URL the watch printed reported back.
expectations: The twelve files land under `src/com/acme/my_cool_app/` and `test/com/acme/my_cool_app/` — NOT `src/com.acme/my_cool_app/`, which is the natural result of a textual rename and does not back the namespace `shadow-cljs.edn` names.

Every `ns` form and internal require reads `com.acme.my-cool-app.*` (dashes preserved), and `shadow-cljs.edn`'s `:init-fn` is `com.acme.my-cool-app.core/init` — namespace and path agree, so the entry symbol resolves.
`package.json`'s `name` is `my-cool-app` — the artefact segment, lowercased — never the qualified Clojure name `com.acme/my-cool-app`, which npm rejects.
The `<h1>`, the `<title>`, the README `#` heading and the file-header comments carry the coordinate VERBATIM (`com.acme/my-cool-app`), not the namespace form.

The identity is settled BEFORE the first file is written: an artefact segment npm cannot take (a leading `_` or `.`, a character outside `a-z 0-9 - _ . ~`, over 214 characters) is reported and nothing is scaffolded — matching the generator, which throws before it emits.
The run still reaches the terminating `npx shadow-cljs compile app` with exit 0 and reports the URL the watch printed — a custom name changes the identity, not the six steps.
No clarification round is taken: the supplied name is sufficient input, and the zero-interview default holds for the substrate, the pins and everything the author did not name.
